candidate.wheel_availability: Original wheel retained locally; public packets contain its hash and build receipt. Rebuild the pinned source and record a new wheel hash; bit-identical wheels are not promised.

published_baseline.scope: Historical published baseline; predates the FFT energy correction and graph backend. It is not the challenge candidate.

engineering_review.scope: PR #194 implementation and evidence packaging only; not scientific approval or independent review.

evidence_packets.method: Installed-candidate analytic/SciPy reference comparisons; independent graph assembly, seeded negative controls, raw candidate/reference arrays.
Wolfram 15.0.1 independently assembled references compared against the preserved candidate data, not a fresh candidate execution; same AI-assisted authoring context.

challenges.title: FFT kinetic-energy normalization
challenges.claim: The two CPU FFT energy diagnostics agree with analytic unit-norm plane-wave kinetic energy within the registered bounds for the 72 specified grid, length, mass and mode cases.
challenges.model_scope: Periodic rectangular 2-D and 3-D grids; zero potential and coupling; modes below Nyquist. Not arbitrary states or empirical dark-matter validation.
challenges.falsification_target: A reproducible in-scope energy or norm error above its registered bound; distinguish it from the already rejected missing-cell-measure control.
limitations: Only analytic plane waves in the fixed parameter grid were checked.
No interacting-energy, mask-conservation, physical calibration or universal correctness claim follows.
unresolved_questions: Are cell measure, normalization and units interpreted correctly?
Which additional states and potential/coupling regimes need a separately preregistered test?

challenges.title: Finite graph mass, stiffness and spectral subspaces
challenges.claim: For the 15 specified small finite graphs, candidate topology, mass/stiffness matrices, spectra, complete weighted eigenspace projectors and tail diagnostics agree with the independently assembled references within registered bounds.
challenges.model_scope: Experimental CPU finite-graph model, levels 0–2, Neumann or principal-restriction Dirichlet boundary, three lengths; level-zero Dirichlet excluded. Distinct from rectangular Fractal SSFM.
challenges.falsification_target: An in-scope topology/boundary mismatch or numerical bound violation, using complete degenerate eigenspaces rather than individual eigenvectors.
limitations: Agreement implements the same declared modeling convention; it does not establish that convention as physically correct.
Wolfram tail power is reconstructed from retained candidate projectors, not a new invocation of the candidate tail method.
No continuum convergence, cross-level equivalence, quantum advantage, or hosted graph execution is established.
unresolved_questions: Is the cell-incidence mass measure appropriate for the intended finite model?
Is Dirichlet principal restriction the intended boundary treatment?
How should the L^-2 factor and (5/3)^level stiffness convention be interpreted?
What multilevel comparison and continuum target, if any, are defensible?

challenges.title: Graph evolution accuracy and temporal refinement
challenges.claim: For the two specified level-2 finite-graph initial-value problems, linear propagation, nonlinear trajectories, norm drift and resolved temporal-refinement orders meet the registered bounds against the independent references.
challenges.model_scope: One Dirichlet and one Neumann case, L=1, mass=1.3, coupling=0.7, fixed quadrant fields, T=0.01 and 4/8/16/32 steps; complex phase retained in trajectory error.
challenges.falsification_target: An in-scope trajectory/linear/norm failure or resolved refinement order outside the registered interval. Reference disagreement or unresolved refinement must be reported as inconclusive.
limitations: Norm conservation alone is not trajectory accuracy; the phase-perturbed negative control demonstrates this.
Short-time finite-model agreement does not establish long-time stability, continuum convergence, or physical applicability.
SciPy and Wolfram references are AI-assisted maintainer evidence, not independent human assessment.
unresolved_questions: Are the initial state, quadrant fields and nonlinear equation the intended model?
Is the reference separation sufficient to interpret the measured order?
Which longer-time or stronger-coupling regimes should be tested prospectively?
